ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$. Points $F$ and $C$ are on $\odot O$, and arc $AF = \text{arc} FC = \text{arc} BC$. Connect $AC$ and $AF$. Through point $C$, draw $CD \perp AF$ to intersect the extended line of $AF$ at point $D$, with the foot of the perpendicular being $D$. $CD$ is a tangent of $\odot O$; If $CD = 2\sqrt{3}$, what is the radius of $\odot O$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect BC as shown in the figure. \\
Since AB is the diameter, it follows that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Since $\overset{\frown}{AF} = \overset{\frown}{FC} = \overset{\frown}{BC}$, it follows that $\angle BOC = \frac{1}{3} \times 180^\circ = 60^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$, thus $\angle DAC = 30^\circ$. In $\triangle ADC$, given $CD = 2\sqrt{3}$, it follows that $AC = 2CD = 4\sqrt{3}$.\\
In $\triangle ACB$, $BC = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}AC = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \times 4\sqrt{3} = 4$, therefore $AB = 2BC = 8$.\\
Hence, the radius of the circle $O$ is $\boxed{4}$.

Then F = (-R/2, √3R/2) and C = (R/2, √3R/2). The line AF has slope √3, so its equation is y = √3(x + R). The tangent at C has slope -1/√3, matching the drawn CD perpendicular to AF. Therefore CD is the perpendicular distance from C to line AF. Compute this distance: |√3(R/2) - √3R/2 + √3R| / 2 = √3R/2. Set √3R/2 = 2√3, giving R = 4.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$. Points $F$ and $C$ are on $\odot O$, and arc $AF = \text{arc }FC = \text{arc }BC$. Connect $AC$ and $AF$. Through point $C$, draw $CD \perp AF$ so that it intersects the extension of line $AF$ at point $D$, with $D$ as the foot of the perpendicular. $CD$ is a tangent of $\odot O$. If $CD = 2\sqrt{3}$, what is the radius of $\odot O$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $BC$ as shown in the figure. \\
Since $AB$ is the diameter, it follows that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Since $\overset{\frown}{AF} = \overset{\frown}{FC} = \overset{\frown}{BC}$, it follows that $\angle BOC = \frac{1}{3} \times 180^\circ = 60^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$, thus $\angle DAC = 30^\circ$. In $\triangle ADC$, given $CD = 2\sqrt{3}$, it follows that $AC = 2CD = 4\sqrt{3}$.\\
In $\triangle ACB$, $BC = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}AC = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \times 4\sqrt{3} = 4$, therefore $AB = 2BC = 8$.\\
Hence, the radius of the circle $O$ is $\boxed{4}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the center of the circle is O, AB is a horizontal diameter, A is on the left, B is on the right, and O is on AB. F and C are located on the upper semicircular arc, A, F, and D are on the same straight line, and D is on the outward extension of AF; connect from C to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating that CD is perpendicular to AD (that is, perpendicular to the extension line of AF). AC has been connected in the figure, and BC can be connected additionally.
Reasoning: From the given conditions, arc AF, arc FC, and arc CB are equal, and they exactly form the upper semicircular arc from A to B, so the central angle of each arc is 180°÷3=60°. Therefore the inscribed angle ∠BAC subtended by arc BC is 30°; the inscribed angle ∠FAC subtended by arc FC is 30°. Since AD and AF are on the same line, ∠DAC=30°. In right triangle ADC, ∠D=90°, ∠A=30°, and CD=2√3. The side CD opposite 30° is equal to half of the hypotenuse AC, so AC=2·CD=4√3. Also because AB is a diameter, ∠ACB=90°. In right triangle ACB, ∠A=30°, therefore BC=AC/√3=4√3/√3=4, and AB=2BC=8. The radius of the circle is half of AB, so the radius is 4.
